video_title: Draymond Green Reacts To 76ers FIRING Daryl Morey, Pistons INSANE OT Ending & Dylan Harper Breakout

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA Combine is a complete waste of time
quotes.quote: The NBA Combine is taking place right now in Chicago and man, do I remember those days. The NBA Combine is, is cool because you kind of get to know some guys that you, you know of, right? But you don't really know. One relationship that I remember first beginning at the NBA Combine, and has stretched throughout the tenure of our careers, is that's the first time I met Dame Lillard. And immediately right then we hit it off. I think it was just a respect for, like, I didn't come from a smaller school, he come from a smaller school, but almost being overlooked. And you kind of just like understood, had an understanding for each other, right? And so I think that's one of the good things about the Combine. If I'm honest though, it's, it's one of the shittiest days of your, or shittiest few days of your career, because you're under this huge microscope. You're doing all these meetings where you get asked these dumbass questions and they're just trying to, like, catch you up and stuff. You're going to all these medical appointments where they only want to red flag you and drop your draft stock. Like, it's kind of this thing that doesn't, you know, it, it, it doesn't add a bunch of value, but it, but it subtracts it. You know, and I'll get into that. But anyway, we had some newsworthy performances. When I came through the NBA Combine, we didn't play five-on-five, which I think would have actually helped my draft stock tremendously. We only did workouts, and I am just not a big workout guy. Never have been. Put me in a game, let's go. Workouts, nah. Right? And so we only did drill stuff, which I think was actually to my detriment. It's good if they play five-on-five now, and which Baylor's Cameron Carr had 30 points in a scrimmage. Measured at a 6'4", 6'4" height, 7'0" wingspan. Like, the measurables was great to have 30 in the scrimmage. Great day for him. Michigan had a couple guys who had stand-out measurables in drills and different things. Maraj Johnson Jr., Drew Bam Adebayo comparisons. Measured at 6'9" with a 7'4" wingspan. Now, here's a situation where that's going to help this guy, right? Like, you watch him play at Michigan, wasn't really one of the focal points, but was very important and key to them winning. And then he comes out with these measurables, 6'9", 7'4" wingspan. Like, he's a lot bigger than, I'm sure, everybody thought he was. Top performer in pro lane drill, top performer in 3/4 court sprint, and the max vertical jump. Right? And so, here's a situation, like, now because of his measurables, he's been compared to Bam Adebayo. One thing I can assure you, no one was comparing him to Bam Adebayo before the Combine. So, there's a situation where it wins for you. You know, Michigan's Adem Bona measured in at 7'3" with a 7'6" wingspan, 9'9" standing reach, tied with Mark Williams for second largest standing reach in Combine history, only behind Tacko Fall. That's something that's going to help him out. Right? Now, what'll be interesting with Maraj is, we're going back to the day and age where we're drafting big men, uh, really high. And due to the success of Joker, Joel. But, what's going to get interesting and tricky with drafting big men now is, your big men's going to, like, the, the person you're going to be drafting your big man to guard now is going to be Victor Wembanyama, which is going to be interesting. Because you're not going to be able to draft big logs, but you're going to need the size. But there's no Victor Wembanyamas anywhere else. So, how you're drafting the big man and why is actually going to get very interesting. Virginia Tech's Toby Laoye recorded the second best standing vertical in NBA Combine history at 40 and a half inches. All great things. All these people could help themselves. Now, Kingston Flemmings, um, kind of tested a bit small, 6'2.5", 6'3.5" wingspan, which looks tough when you're going up against a guard who measured at 6'2.5" and a 6'7.5" wingspan in Darius Acuff. Right? So, now people start using things like that against you. The reality is, I don't put much stock into the Combine. In some situations like these I just mentioned where they can help you, but I think the Combine is kind of a technicality and a complete waste of time. I will say the NBA Combine is not as beneficial as the NFL Combine. Somebody can go to the NFL Combine, test out the waters and go from a fifth-round pick to a second-round pick. That ain't really happening in the NBA Combine, which I think is why it's actually pointless.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Daryl Morey's exit from Philly was inevitable
quotes.quote: Daryl Morey was fired by the Sixers. My guy, former Warriors General Manager who drafted yours truly, Bob Myers will oversee the 76ers basketball department in the interim. He will lead the search for the franchise's new executive. And quite honestly, what I do know is, if you're able to be in the running for this job, you're lucky. Because you get Bob Myers as a sounding board. You get one of the greatest GMs as a sounding board when you're stepping into this job. And what better tool can you have? It's like Bob's a goat, right? Like, to have Jerry West as a sounding board, what an incredible tool that was for front office members to have, whether that was Bob, whether that was Lawrence Frank, or dating back to Jerry's days as General Manager, President. Like, what an incredible thing you get to have in taking this job, and you got Bob Myers as a sounding board. Someone who's not afraid to go for it. Like, that's incredible. And I think whoever gets this job, it'll be very beneficial. Whether that's just beneficial during your tenure with the 76ers or as you move forward, you've been under that tutelage. Very, very beneficial. Now, in other news, Bob Myers is to, has been to Daryl Morey almost what Michael Jordan was to, like, Stockton and Malone. Like, you are, you've done great work. I mean, I'm not saying Daryl Morey is Stockton or Malone, but you'll get the reference in a second. But you've done some great work, right? You traded for James Harden when nobody believed, gave him a max contract, and then James Harden proceeded to become who he's become. You built a team with the Houston Rockets that was a very good roster that was built to beat the Golden State Warriors. It didn't quite happen, but built a good team. You go to Philly and sign Tyrese Maxey to a max deal, right? Like, done some good things in Philly. Just can't quite get over the hump. And Bob Myers, he, Daryl Morey couldn't get over the hump due to teams that Bob Myers was putting together. And now, um, Daryl Morey is going to lose his role as the President of Basketball Operations due to Bob Myers, um, making the basketball decisions in Philly, uh, which he's well deserved, he's more than capable and well deserved and should be making basketball decisions anywhere. Uh, but Daryl Morey just kind of keeps running into Bob Myers, and it's unfortunate. Um, I know Bob means well, but Morey kind of had this from coming. You had the whole James Harden situation that got butchered a couple years ago. The writing was kind of on the wall once Bob got announced to President of all the sports, uh, that Josh Harris and David Blitzer own. You're talking the New Jersey Devils, you're talking the Philadelphia 76ers, you're talking the Washington Commanders. Bob has a say in all of that. And so you kind of knew once that was announced that this was kind of going to happen.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Check on your people, tomorrow ain't promised
quotes.quote: Also, big hit to the NBA family as Brandon Clarke and Jason Collins passed away within the last few days. Man, you know, it's, like, obviously, with Jason Collins, I have, you know, I've been around him due to Jarron Collins being our assistant coach, so Jason would come around, always super pleasant, always super nice, very easy to talk to, super outgoing. And, you know, for the last couple years have struggled with a bout with cancer and ultimately passed away two days ago. And so I want to send my love and well wishes and prayers up, but love to the Collins family. I can't imagine, you know, you always hear the love of a twin. You know, and as a twin for Jarron to lose the other half of yourself, obviously not his wife, that's your better half, but twin, it's different. And I can't imagine what he's going through, so I really send my love and respect to the Collins family. And Brandon Clarke, who I've had the opportunity to play against, play against in meaningful series, and just kind of watching the young fella grow. I know him and Jarron Jackson, who obviously I'm, it's my young Spartan dog, um, had a very close relationship. And, uh, you know, it's, it's unfortunate because, you know, I've also heard over the last couple years him talk about the strain that the going through the injury was putting on his life, and then to come back last year and only play two games. You know, this stuff is serious, man. And I'm not implying nothing other than just check on your people. Make sure your people good. You love somebody, check on them. Because tomorrow just ain't promised. So I send my well wishes and love to Brandon Clarke, the Clarke family, the Memphis Grizzlies organization and family, all his friends and loved ones. Can't imagine. Can't imagine. Don't want to imagine. So, just want to send my love.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Kerr's decision to return was a grind
quotes.quote: Steve Kerr talked to ESPN about his decision to return in this past season. What I can say about that is, I actually believe that. You know, if you just think about his energy kind of leading up to it, you know, he was saying all the right things and doing all the right things, but it was just a grind. You know, you're going through, there's no Steph, there's no Jimmy, there's no Moses. And you're kind of going through the wringer, and you kind of feel like the writing is on the wall. Now, I think a part of that could be, you want to also mentally prepare yourself, right? Things aren't going well. Don't really know if Steph's coming back. And you kind of just want to mentally prepare yourself for the worst. Then after winning that Clipper game, it's, man, it's crazy because I walked out of that game, I'm like, this is why you play. Right? Like, this is the reason, these type of moments, this is why you do it. And so, I understand how that could be reinvigorating for someone. Because it's, it's that adrenaline, it's that feeling that, that pushes you through all the tough times. It's that, it's that thing that makes you want to keep going and want to do it again. And so, completely understood that. Congrats to Steve on signing his contract and being back as the Golden State Warriors head coach. I think, you know, big deal, obviously, to put that behind, and move forward and kind of know the path, at least for the next two years, I think is, uh, is pretty big time. So, congrats to Steve on head coach. Also want to say thank you to Terry Stotts and Jerry Stackhouse. Man, Jerry Stackhouse, I'm salty to see go. Just been able over the last two years to build a relationship, a mutual respect, a brotherhood. Like, I tell Stack all the time, man, you remind me so much of my Uncle Benny. Sound like my Uncle Benny, the things they say, how they go at things. And so, just having that familiarity, kind of drew me to him right away. And, uh, forever grateful. Obviously, the relationship don't stop here. But it's going to suck to see him, not see him walk in on a daily basis. Uh, but the things I've learned from him over the last couple years, forever grateful for. Also, it's my golf buddy. Been helping me a lot on the golf course. That'll continue, but shout out to my man Stack. Appreciate you, man.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs' young talent is dynamic and impressive
quotes.quote: Now we'll get into the playoffs. The San Antonio Spurs beat the Timberwolves 126-97 to take a 3-2 series lead. And Wemby completely dominated. Keldon Johnson returned to form that won him Sixth Man of the Year. And Dylan Harper does something else every game that makes you think how bright the San Antonio Spurs' future is going to be. Um, now, San Antonio completely controlled this game pretty much the entire game, except for a four or five minute stretch where the Timberwolves took a 15-point deficit and tied the game at 61-61. Only for the San Antonio Spurs to go on an incredible run, pretty much a 31-7 run. Um, 32-7 run, which ultimately put them up at one point 93-68. Just when you thought Minnesota had found their footing, was about to make it a game, the Spurs just took off. And it just goes to show kind of how dynamic this team is. You get Wemby, goes to the bench, and Keldon Johnson starts playing well. Dylan Harper, I, I didn't get to see him play much in college, but every time I see him play in the NBA, he does something that's more and more impressive to me. Something to where you like, yo, two years from now, this kid, like, he just keeps getting better. And it's unassuming, right? Like, it's not, it's not crazy flashy, except he'll mix you fast. You know, it's not like he's blazing fast speed, except once he get going downhill, you can't catch up to him. Like, it kind of looks a bit deceiving, but he's so nice. So nice. And with him playing like, I, I still think like, and obviously he's a rookie, he's still figuring it out. Like, this is his first playoff series. But as he get more and more comfortable over the next couple years, he has not taken that step of like, yo, I am the guy. I am that guy. Not that he'll be the guy because Victor Wembanyama's there. Stephon Castle's there. But I am one of the guys, like, really one of them. He don't even have that mindset yet, which is going to make him even better player. You know, so I, I, I thought it's been extremely impressive to watch during his playoffs. He has the most bench points in the playoffs, second youngest guard ever to record multiple double-doubles in the playoffs, passing only Derrick Rose. Right? Like, when you start looking, just take a step back and look at Dylan Harper, I think he's extremely special. Extremely special. You know, I think, um, you look at the trio of Wemby, Castle, and Harper, and you got to imagine, these young guys stay healthy, keep egos in check, because sometimes egos can get involved, and they don't seem like the type of guys, I don't think the Spurs really draft the type of guys that ego get involved, but people do change. But as long as ego don't get involved, you look at these three guys. They have size amongst all of them. Ball handling amongst all of them. They have shooting. They have defense. They have a point guard. They have everything that you would need to build a foundation within those three guys. And then now you just will always need to plug and play. Wow. Not to mention, you know, to have Coach Mitch Johnson, to have a sounding board, speaking of sounding boards, we spoke about Bob Myers. To have a sounding board like Greg Popovich. Coach Pop, who is reportedly involved in the Spurs' film session after Game 1 loss to the Wolves. Met with the team after their Game 4 loss. Like, to have someone that you know that all y'all, you keep hearing Wemby say, 'We don't got the experience, we don't care.' Because when you can turn to a Greg Popovich, and, yes, he's not in there every day, but he's around and all the times that you need, that's a very confident feeling because he's going to like Steve Kerr, know all the right things to say and when to say them. Right? So, where Mitch Johnson may not understand, just only because he hasn't been in this situation. Not because he's not a great coach, because he is a great coach. But you only know what you know. You only know what you've been through. And so, to have that sounding board like, oh, well, I remember when we went through this with that, this is how y'all need to be approaching this. What a special place. What a special place that Coach Popovich has built, that they've continued to grow and enhance. Absolutely incredible. You know, so you got to ask yourself the question, with all of those things, can you extend this series to a Game 7? The answer is yes, you can. Um, and the reason you can is because, as inexperienced as this team is that we just spoke about, they don't necessarily know how to close. Now, they have closed, but they don't necessarily know how to close. Now, ultimately they will win this series. Can Minnesota extend it? It's one thing, but what they must play at is, these guys don't know how to close. Let's come out, punch first, punch second, they're going to punch third, let's punch fourth, because they don't know how to close, simply because they haven't been there. In comes De'Aaron Fox. If they want to close this series in six, Fox is going to have to take over the game at some point. Because he is the one that has been in these situations, obviously not to get to the Conference Finals, but he's been in these situations, playoff situations, where you need one to close. Fox has been in the situation. So he's felt that pressure before, he knows what it's like. I don't know that they can extend it. However, like I said, Fox is the key. If they're going to close it in six, it must be De'Aaron Fox taking over the reins.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Cade Cunningham ran out of gas
quotes.quote: The Cavs beat the Pistons 117-113 in overtime to take a 3-2 series lead. Cleveland ultimately trailed by nine with like three minutes to go. Um, closed the game on a 9-0 run to force OT and the big three. Um, and I must be honest, I'm sitting there watching this game and like, I couldn't believe it. You got to give Evan Mobley credit. Seven straight points to force OT. And the big three. Um, only to then go on to outscore the Pistons 14-10 in overtime. James, second straight big game, 30 points, eight rebounds, six assists, three blocks. A lot of talk about James. A lot, oh, he can't do this, he can't do that. A lot of talk about him. I said a couple episodes ago, y'all aren't giving the Pistons credit for the defense that they were playing. However, which further backs up what I said, James has figured out the defense. Because when you are a great scorer, when you are a great player, when you are James Harden, you've seen every defense, including guys standing behind you guarding to sing you to the rim. You've seen every defensive coverage you can possibly imagine. Although they're super athletic, although they're super young, length. You've seen every defense you can possibly imagine. At some point, you get comfortable and you figure out the reads and you figure it out, you figure out the timing. And I think James has just figured it out now. So much talk, oh man, his legacy's going to be over, like, stop. It's crazy. It's James Harden. And he's shown that these last couple games. We talk about swing players, guys swinging the series. Max Strus, 20 points, eight rebounds, but not only that. I said earlier in this series, Dean Wade ain't the answer, guarding Cade. Can't do it. And although Cade had a big game, Max Strus picked him up full court. Cade finished with 39. And although he had a big game, down the stretch, when the, when the Cavs were on that 9-0 run to force OT, Cade didn't have the ball. And to me, it looked like he was a bit tired. And what it was reminiscent of was watching Anthony Edwards, um, was it a year ago, two years ago, year ago, when they played the Dallas Mavericks. And it just seemed like to me in that Conference Finals that Ant-Man ran out of gas. And that man spoke on that. He said, I got to get in better shape. Ran out of gas. What it looks like the other night was Cade ran out of gas. Now, we speaking of swing players, Max Strus picked him up full court every time. Made basket, Max Strus right there. And so I think over the course of time, ultimately in that game, with the overtime, Cade played 48 minutes. And I think he just ran out of gas. And so, when you look at the team, you know, you speak on the Minnesota Timberwolves when with Ant-Man, ball dominant, heavy, heavy, need to make every play for the team. Same position Cade's been in. And I think, you know, I, I watched that for years with James Harden when we were playing the Rockets. And when you're playing that style of basketball, it's just so hard for those guys late to deliver. Our whole game plan will be, yo, James is going to go off. He's probably going to have 20 in the first half. They probably going to be up 20 in the first half. But we just stay the course because he's going to get tired, and we're going to storm. And that's what happened every time. And that's, so that's what was reminiscent of to me. Which just to watch, like, man, this guy who has to make every play offensively, ultimately, I think just ran out of gas. Couldn't close the game out. So then you had other guys taking shots and trying to make plays down the stretch, and it just didn't work. Because ultimately that has to be Cade. But when you got to do it for 48 minutes with a guy picking you up full court every time, I think ultimately he just ran out of gas. And so, how do you combat that? I don't know that it can be combatted right now. Uh, it's probably an off-season thing. They can still win this series, but they're going to have to find a way. And Tobias had a tough game. My thing is, Tobias has been solid, dog. And down the stretch, Tobias didn't really get any touches. Once the game got haywire, you see, you see Cade a little tired. Get, get Tobias a mid-post touch. Even if he doesn't score, he was struggling to shoot, uh, struggling to score with a shot that game. I think he finished the game 6-for-17 or something like that. Even if he doesn't score, it slows the game down. You're up nine points with three minutes to go. Even if you don't score another point, you should win that game. You get that ball to Tobias, Cade naturally slows it down. Cade didn't have the ball. Or Tobias. So everything is just going, going, going. You get that ball to Tobias, it slows the game down. Now you got a 20 to 24 second shot clock that runs off, right? Like, say you get an offensive rebound, it's another 14 seconds. Right? That's managing the game. And so I think if you can get Tobias a post-touch down the stretch, mid-post, let him work and slow the game down. Maybe he don't score. Maybe he get a kick-out for a three. Maybe you get an offensive rebound, or maybe you just waste 24 seconds as opposed to four. It's a big difference. You know, so some of the things I think they need to do down the stretch. I actually thought, um, I thought it was crazy that the NBA came out and said that that that was no, it was a no-call. Um, Ausar Thompson got tripped. Point blank period. Incidental or not, I hate when they say, oh, like, yeah, he did trip him, but it was incidental. Hey man, sometimes I foul, and I didn't mean to. It was incidental. That's the nature of basketball. Sometimes you may trip someone and you didn't try to, you still tripped them. That's a foul. So I don't know where, or how, it's like, oh man, that wasn't a foul. He had a guy up ahead, he could have hit and got a quick shot off. But he got tripped and lost the ball. I thought that was crazy. Jalen Duren struggled a bit in these playoffs. And it's interesting because everybody's like, yo, did he, is he losing himself a lot of money? In reality is, say if his max is 210. What's going to happen is, without an offer sheet, he'll get anywhere from 160 to 180 from the Pistons. Everybody's saying, oh man, is this mental, why is he struggling like this? And the reality is this. When you get in the playoffs, the thing that you do best is taken away in the first round, maybe sometimes depending on the first round opponent. Maybe not. But by the second round, the thing you do best and sometimes the second best thing is gone. Now you got to do other things, which is why you see so many guys struggle in the playoffs. And so, Jalen Duren averaged 19 and a half points in the regular season. Well, he get four or five lobs a game. Once you get in a playoff series, and a team goes, yo, when somebody drive, we're not stepping up off his body. We're not giving up those lobs. And all of a sudden, you go from four or five lobs a game to one if you're lucky, that will drop your scoring average from 19 and a half to 10-11 points a game. Which is where Jalen Duren is. And so, ultimately, what will have to happen is, this summer, he's going to have to work on what, what are you going to get to when you can't get the lobs? What are you going to get to when it all ain't working? What's your go-to? Right? That's what he's ultimately going to have to work on because, you know, you're in these Finals now. It reminds me of when we're playing the Houston Rockets against Clint Capela. Clint Capela was one of the best lob threats in the league during that time. Our whole game plan, they drive, don't step up off Clint Capela's body, take the lobs away. That cut his average in half. Right? It's the same thing Jalen Duren's going through right now. They're taking some of the lobs away. They're taking some of the lobs away. Wemby's going through some of it. They're taking some of the lobs away. Wemby just does so many other things that he's still going to get to it. But, if you don't do all those other things, and now they're just taking all the lobs away, that will cut your points per game if you're Jalen Duren by 8 to 10 points. And so, you know, I think what the Pistons' focus has to be with him is like, yo, we need rebounds, we need defense, we need this. And then get some offensive rebounds and put-backs, right? Like, impact the game. Don't necessarily have to come off a lob because they ain't given that to us, but, I don't know that you can win at a very high level with Jalen Duren not in the game. I just don't, I don't know that he's an All-Star for a reason. And he's up for the contract he's up for for a reason. So, they're going to have to figure that out. They're going to need a big Jalen Duren, especially against Jarrett Allen and Evan Mobley. So, hopefully they can figure it out, but it's been rough on him. Uh, still got a chance to change it. It's a beautiful thing about the NBA. You got another game tomorrow.
